label: final copy output in length-4 sequences (copy-phase end feature)
explanation: Fires almost entirely in the copy phase (99.8% of mass). It never fires at the delimiter and almost never in the original phase. It is concentrated at the last output step of short sequences: recall_idx==3 carries 78% of mass, to_go==0 carries 77%, and L=4 carries 72% (t=7, the final step of an L=4 sequence). The top activations are all at the last step of L=4 sequences, often with weaker activation on the preceding copy steps. Inputs that are repeats of earlier tokens (in_first==0) carry nearly all the mass. Magnitude depends on token identity: sequences containing e, x, q, n (and, for out_tok, w/e/n/y) give the largest values, but restricting to those tokens raises precision to 0.80 while recall drops sharply. It also fires weakly at the final or second-to-last copy steps of L=5 sequences and sporadically at late copy steps of longer sequences. About 40% of L=4 final steps do not activate, and token identity explains part of that. The predicate is position-based, and the token-dependent modulation leaves precision and recall incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: x, e, q, n, t, u; least: m, i, a, r) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: w, e, v, y; input phase: ; delimiter step: ); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, t=5, L=4 & t=7.
